answer: Jittered arrival corridors. Each identity must route its first N actions through a vault that emits requests along a randomized timing envelope; the coordinator checks that arrival interleavals fit that envelope and rejects bursts outside it. A haven of valid identities is one whose envelopes overlap only within statistical tolerance. The cost to an attacker is serialization: forged identities cannot share one fast pipeline without producing detectable burst jade, so each fake must wait out its own envelope, multiplying wall-clock time and per-identity compute by N.
